US Dealer Buys New Lamborghini Temerario, Puts It Up for Sale, Refuses $366,000
17 photos
Photo: Cars&Bids
While Lamborghini was preparing to pull the wraps off the Spyder version of the Temerario, this dealer was refusing a lot of money for their Lamborghini.
Truth be told, they probably wouldn’t even have broken even if they had accepted the offer, because the total suggested retail price of this stealthy-looking Italian supercar was over $470,000 as per the attached window sticker. The offer was $366,000, as this was the highest bid when the gavel hit the table recently (November 18, 2026) on Cars&Bids. And with the reserve not being met, the vehicle failed to change hands.
This Lamborghini Temerario is a 2026 model said to pack roughly $82,000 in options alone. It has around 300 miles (~ km) under its belt, a Nero Noctis exterior, a Nero Ade interior, and a clean Oregon title. The mileage is accurate, and it hasn’t been involved in any accidents, the Carfax report reveals. Moreover, due to the very low mileage, this Italian supercar, which sits below the Revuelto in the Raging Bull’s current portfolio, hasn’t required any servicing yet.
Photo: Cars&Bids Power is supplied by a twin-turbo 4.0-liter V8 engine assisted by three electric motors. The plug-in hybrid assembly produces 907 hp (920 ps/677 kW) in total, enabling 0-62 mph (0-100 kph) in 2.7 seconds, and a 213 mph (343 kph) top speed. The model features an eight-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission for fast gear shifts, and all-wheel drive.
Some of the gear mentioned in the ad includes the 20-inch front and 21-inch (Velador) wheels, the Alleggerita Package, carbon ceramic brakes, and a nose-lift system. The sports seats, a passenger display, a reversing camera, and leather and Corsa Tex upholstery are also mentioned in the ad. We should also tell you that there is satin PPF on the outside of this Lamborghini Temerario , an that the front splitter has some scuffs on it. The tires are said to carry 2025 and 2026 date codes.
In addition to the supercar, the next owner will also get the window sticker, a charging cable, two keys, a car cover, and the usual lecture. So, if you fancy the look of this Lamborghini Temerario (I know I do!) and want to make yourself an early Christmas gift, then you should reach out to the vendor and make an offer. After all, what’s the worse that they can say? No?
Those interested in the pictured Lamborghini Temerario can check it out in more detail here on Cars&Bids, and before clicking that link, how much do you think this machine is worth? For the record, the 2027 MY starts from almost $400,000, and it tends to sell from well over $300,000 to in excess of half a million dollars on the used car market.
